title: Grateful Dead Live at Crisler Arena on 1989-04-05
source: Healy Ultra Mix - sbd+aud> cm> dat> cd

ai_review.summary: Excellent matrix recording captures a blues‑heavy Ann Arbor show with standout Sampson→Cumberland and a memorable Terrapin→Drums, though the set feels short and low on improvisation.
ai_review.review: The sbd‑matrix source is praised for its crystal‑clear mix and clean instrument separation, making this a very listenable document of the 1989 Ann Arbor concert.  The performance leans heavily into blues numbers – US Blues, Sampson, Cumberland and China Doll – with several reviewers highlighting the surprise US Blues close and the Sampson→Cumberland transition as high points, while noting a relatively short second set and limited jamming overall.

ai_rating.rationale: Recording quality is consistently rated excellent (≈4.5‑5★) while show quality is described as decent but not spectacular (≈3.0‑3.5★). Weighted average (70% show, 30% recording) yields ~3.8★.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers repeatedly call the sound "great", "killer" and "crisp"; the matrix blend is described as clean with good instrument balance and no major drop‑outs.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Set 1 opens strong with Stranger→Franklin's and a surprise US Blues closer; Set 2 is shorter than expected, featuring Sampson>Cumberland and the usual late‑night sequence (Terrapin → Drumz).  The concert leans heavily on blues cuts (five in total) and lacks extended improvisation.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Lead breaks on Stranger and Cumberland praised; long solo on China Doll noted, though a few reviewers say his tone isn’t as electrifying later in the set.
band_member_comments.Phil: New bass rig mentioned positively; anchors Let It Grow and keeps pace with Jerry during Sampson/Cumberland.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent’s shoulder‑shrug solo on Candyman highlighted; overall keyboard work described as solid.
band_member_comments.Drums: Standard drum segment noted; Drumz/Space transitions described as tight.
